strain accommodation during rifting is a complex process involving both faulting and magma intrusion, but with the relative contribution from each process varying with rifting stage, crustal rheology and tectonic setting.
strain is released by a combination of slow slip and magma intrusion during the initial stages in the development of a continental rift.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 2007 Mw 5.8 seismic event in the East African rift is an example of strain release by aseismic slip on a normal faults and subsequent dyke intrusion.
the 2007 seismic event in the Natron rift was caused by the accumulation of stress over time, which was relieved by a combination of aseismic fault slip and dyke intrusion.
the strain during the 2007 seismic event in the Natron rift was accommodated by slow slip on the main fault and by dyking, with the latter being the dominant mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
strain is partitioned between aseismic and seismic processes during the early phases of continental rifting.
magma intrusion and slow slip can be a significant part of the deformation budget of young rifts.
the initial stage of continental rifting is characterized by strain accommodation by slow slip, dyking and faulting, rather than just faulting.
